pairs.subject: data-video-virality
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/idea.ts:84 A stats idea comes in through the ideas door as case/title/hook/unit/kind/illustrative data plus optional steps. Nothing records granularity, span, entity count, expected lead changes, dated events, a measure or comparables, so none of the subject's gates can run before the operator triages.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/idea.ts:93 The format is classified (level-race, cumulative-race, counter, ranking, share), but no field counts real steps or entities and no shape is refused. 'counter' is a single-value format, and it is accepted. The data is illustrative, so the step floor is never checked against data that can actually be obtained.

lib/foundry/scout/idea.ts:91 The hook only has to be non-empty text of at most 200 chars. There is no keep-watching rationale that must name at least two dates and two entities, and the technique names exactly this as a failure.

lib/foundry/scout/idea.ts:96 Steps are optional free text, minimum 1, with no date or on-screen effect. Nothing enforces the 5-event floor inside the animated span, or how the events spread across it.

lib/foundry/scout/reelDoor.ts:58 Partly realized: what-if sources get an on-screen fiction label (reelTaste.ts:16 sourceLine). But a what-if needs only a premise. No real-data end year, stated model, horizon at most twice the baseline, or 2100 cap is recorded or refused, and reelDoor.ts:15-22 accepts 'what if fantasy scenarios', which the technique fails as invented narrative.

lib/foundry/scout/ideaRepeat.ts:41 The only repeat guard at the ideas door checks character briefs. Stats ideas pass untouched (the header says 'every other target passes untouched'), and no measure is stored to screen subject+measure+span.

packages/producers/src/scout-reels/define.ts:95 A what-if source carries only a premise and a name line. No baseline end year, model or horizon is checked before the seat authors it.
